mechanics.name: Ascension 1: Slow Foundations
mechanics.description: New player-owned factories need two complete economic days to become operational.
paragraphs: Select Ascension 0: Normal or Ascension 1: Slow Foundations before starting. Difficulty belongs to this run; it is not an unlock, prestige reward, stacking curse or permanent bonus. Ascension 0 preserves instant construction without a construction delay.

At Ascension 1, ordering a new player facility pays its full cost immediately and creates an under-construction site without advancing the day. Two successful AdvanceDay operations complete it. The site skips automatic procurement, production and sales throughout both days, including completion day's automatic phases.

A two-day bakery ordered on day 0 completes after day 2's voyage phase and first becomes eligible to produce on day 4. Its own stock, enabled state and capacity must still permit the batch. Completion grants no free inputs, does not charge again, and is recorded as a zero-cash event.

Manual local warehouse buying/selling, storage and physically docked owned transfers remain legal during construction under the normal cash, stock and capacity rules. They cannot produce early. Already-built starter facilities, including the Industrial Consortium bakery, retain their original schedule and grant provenance; later purchases still wait. This narrow industrial penalty need not affect every strategy equally.

mechanics.name: Cargo and storage capacity
mechanics.description: Every physical item uses one unit of ship or private storage capacity.
paragraphs: Capacity counts all commodities together. A hold containing several kinds of goods has less room for the next shipment even if the selected commodity's quantity is small.

Buying and transfers respect available stock and receiving capacity. Production checks the complete resulting private inventory before consuming inputs. A blocked batch does not partly consume materials.
Maximum trade quantities reflect current stock, exact payment, liquidity, and capacity. They remain previews and cannot authorize a remote transaction.

New v3 runs pool company storage per town. Capacity sums all granted and paid local facility warehouse capacities, including pending sites. Operational facilities with the same recipe add their output ceilings together. Pending sites provide storage but cannot produce early. Legacy saves keep their separate warehouses.

mechanics.name: Ordered cargo itineraries
mechanics.description: Plan mixed cargo and ordered market or company-stock work through two to four towns.
paragraphs: Fleet > Route planner is also reachable from a selected owned ship's deck or Harbor. Choose an owned ship, then draft two to four unique town stops with one to eight ordered actions each, at most 24 total. Select a stop card and enter several goods in its Unload / Sell / Load / Buy quantity grid. Blank or zero removes an instruction. New stops use that disposal-first order, then stable commodity ID order; reopened routes keep their exact order. Advanced limits & execution order exposes individual limits and ordering, including separate repeated instructions. Drafting and inspecting pause playback without changing stocks, cash or time.

Buy and Sell exchange the named good with the public market for its exact bulk price. Load and Unload transfer owned stock between the actual docked ship and its company town stock without payment. No owned facility means no town warehouse, but you can apply the plan before building. Missing storage skips or waits as configured; later ordinary construction lets the unchanged route use the real store. A route never creates goods, storage or buildings. Different goods can remain aboard together within the combined hold capacity; unmentioned goods are never discarded.

Every action executes once per visit, choosing the largest whole quantity between its minimum and maximum that current stock, capacity and real funds permit. Maximum is an order cap, not a hold target. A partial qualifying order advances once. Below minimum, Skip continues with no transaction; Wait keeps that exact action and stops. Earlier completed buys or transfers never repeat because another instruction waits.

Buy limits include maximum marginal ask, company cash reserve and a per-order spending cap; Sell uses a minimum marginal bid. Price zero means unrestricted and a blank spending cap means unrestricted within actual funds. Loading can preserve a fractional town-stock reserve. Maximum and minimum cargo quantities are whole units; coin and warehouse reserves support four decimal places. Remote quotes describe current conditions, not reserved future prices or permission to move goods.

Each ship can use eight itinerary operations per economic day, counting successful orders, intentional skips and departure. Eight commands can leave departure for tomorrow. Repeated Run dockside actions, pause and save/load cannot reset this budget. Ships keep the ordinary priority and ID order, real voyages and shared company cash; a blocked ship does not prevent the other ships from acting.

Apply draft assigns the route and leaves actions paused. Replacing a route requires Manual control, an actual dock included in the new plan, no partially completed old stop and no itinerary operations already performed today. Advance a day after completed work before replacing it. Viewing never requires empty cargo; applying preserves it. Equivalent reapplication keeps progress. Manual travel elsewhere does not reset the next stop; return there before resuming.

Draft Grain–Flour–Bread loop resolves the actual role towns: A unloads two Flour and two Logs and loads up to four Bread; B sells up to four Bread and buys four Grain plus two Logs; C sells four Grain and buys two Flour before returning. All orders use minimum one and Skip. Purchases retain 100 company coins and cap each order at 200. You may apply before building, but must construct the eligible Bakery and fund wages yourself for production; the example creates no stock, facilities or money.

The live planner shows actual dock or voyage, next stop and action, cargo and an authoritative blocker. Expand Cargo, last outcome & daily budget for daily budget and last outcome; inspect an action for current source stock, market funds and quote. Pass count advances when leaving the last listed stop, so an initial middle-stop pass is not a completed circuit. Inspect harbor returns to ordinary trading. Back returns to the prior screen or overlay.

Schema5 retains itinerary format1 plans, exact stop/action/cycle, last outcome and daily budget across mid-stop and mid-voyage saves. Load continues the exact next work; Retry starts fresh with the same identity.

mechanics.name: Challenges and run outcomes
mechanics.description: A challenge ends in victory, deadline defeat, or confirmed voluntary abandonment.
paragraphs: Grand Commission offers one choice from three cards in each of four deterministic category rounds, after exploring the full seeded map. All four selected goals must be currently met by day180 alongside100 liquid company coins. Sandbox has no objective deadline.

The Journal distinguishes cumulative visits, actual funded production and public receipts from reversible net sales, welfare, ownership and value conditions. Buying back a target-market good reverses signed delivery credit. Transfers and previews do not count as sales.

Every complete atomic operation evaluates all conditions. Success takes precedence on the exact deadline; success, failure or confirmed abandonment freezes economic actions. The acknowledgment offers results or frozen inspection, and terminal saves stay frozen.
Retry Same World reconstructs the original identity and assets. Continue restores an explicit local save instead. There is no hidden auto-save or cloud recovery.

mechanics.name: Starting company charters
mechanics.description: Choose one replacement starting package with understandable tradeoffs.
paragraphs: Run setup shows the selected charter's company cash, ship, cargo, facilities, and supplied stock. Merchant liquidity, an industrial foothold, and independent trading flexibility offer different opportunities rather than stacking upgrades.

Cash alone is not starting wealth. A granted factory or useful stock can support production while a larger hold changes shipping opportunities. Compare the whole package and the chosen objective before starting.

Starter assets are initialized explicitly and are not paid purchases during the run. The Industrial Consortium's inherited bakery is already operational even at Ascension 1, while newly purchased sites wait two days. This makes the modifier affect charters differently. A charter cannot change in an active run. Retry Same World restores its complete original run identity and assets.

mechanics.name: Living city accounts and wages
mechanics.description: Household money, market liquidity and company cash have separate owners.
paragraphs: Each living town has a public market account and an aggregate household account. Every company has one cash account. The current economy also has a public treasury and finite external authority: external commerce transfers existing money across the regional boundary, and only an explicit Silver-backed Mint exchange creates new currency. There is no daily allowance or hidden stock repair.

A successful public production batch moves its wage from market to households. Private production moves its wage from the owning company to households. For example, a wage of 10 moves market 40 to 30 and household 20 to 30; no money is created.

If households then buy Bread for an exact order total of 18, household cash becomes 12 and market cash 48. Only the purchased Bread is consumed. Actual quantities use marginal price totals, stock and affordability; a first-unit quote multiplied by quantity is not the bill.

Market insolvency can block your sale even when households still have money. Retail may later fund the market only if food exists, households can afford it and a need is due. Buying locally, exports and private employment can move real funds; none guarantees a recovery day.

Select the town and open Economy for current food shortfalls, production and separate market/household funds. Food affordability & demand reveals exact next-need calculations. Accounts & pricing opens actual wage/retail payments, observed food and fiscal detail. Back retains the town and prior workspace. Missing stock and unaffordable available stock are different constraints.

Modern circulation towns review accounts every four days before public production. Only ready public work can trigger a payroll levy, and households keep twice their next essential food budget. Otherwise food relief requires actual food on the shelf and protects upcoming public payroll. Each direction is limited to the shortfall, 12 coins and 10% of the payer's unreserved cash. The town screen shows recorded reserves, reason, totals and next review. No money or food is created.

mechanics.name: Food, furniture and municipal use
mechanics.description: Different consumers need different goods on explicit schedules.
paragraphs: Bread is the essential household good, due every four days. The current economy uses exact proportional quantities: population 10 needs 0.50, 15 needs 0.75, 20 needs 1.00, 21 needs 1.05 and 30 needs 1.50 Bread. Retail buys only actual affordable stock.

Essentials run before luxuries. Furniture is an infrequent durable household need: one per 80 residents every 24 days when sustained welfare enables it. V2 rounds upward; v3 is proportional with exact residual carry. Luxury spending reserves the exact current price of the next Bread need and cannot spend an unlimited future income.

Municipal Planks are a separate public own-use sink every 12 days. They move no cash to a fictional buyer. Grain, Flour and Logs are industrial inputs and traded goods, not household staples in this model.

Food coverage estimates physical stock divided by scheduled eligible household demand; it is not a guaranteed spending forecast. Goods without household demand show not applicable. Stock-only pricing remains the baseline. Experimental coverage pricing derives bounded stock targets from a seven-day need horizon constrained by actual household funds. Effective pricing parameters stay fixed until the next daily boundary; marginal bid/ask prices still respond to every inventory change.

The command deck and Economy show next Bread due day and exact prospective quantity at current population, including the saved fractional demand remainder. Compare it with current public stock; the separate retail preview uses current quotes and household money. Awaiting first need means no meal has yet been observed. These read-only facts do not promise future stock, funds or prices.

mechanics.name: Population, prosperity and recovery
mechanics.description: Sustained paid food and purchasing power shape bounded city welfare.
paragraphs: Prosperity is a 0 to 100 indicator, not a cash or price multiplier. Up to six recent scheduled food opportunities, including failures to buy, supply a paid-fulfillment share. Current household cash is compared with a reserve benchmark for the next Bread need, priced exactly using current parameters and a hypothetical shelf containing at least that need. This is not a future availability or price promise. Three parts fulfillment and one part purchasing power set the target; prosperity moves toward it by at most three points per observation.

Furniture demand turns on after three consecutive qualifying observations with prosperity at least 65 and full food plus an affordable next-need reserve. It turns off after three consecutive observations with prosperity at most 40 or purchasing power below 25 percent. This hysteresis prevents daily threshold flicker; demand remains subject to real stock and budgets.

Population reviews occur every 12 days after six food observations. At most one resident is gained after sustained adequate food and prosperity at least 65, or lost after sustained severe deprivation and prosperity at most 35. Generated bounds are 10 to 80. New population changes subsequent desired need, not past records.

A city can keep household money yet decline because food is absent; another may have food but no purchasing power. Production inputs, payroll, market buying power and transport can all stall a chain. The model has no guaranteed long-run equilibrium. Grand Commission welfare cards test sustained paid food against the declared baseline, not a one-time shipment.

mechanics.name: Company Value and operating results
mechanics.description: Reference holdings, liquidity and realized earnings are different measures.
paragraphs: V3 Company Value equals company cash plus reference value of every owned cargo and warehouse good, completed ships and factories, and paid pending ship or facility capital. Every store and asset appears once. Reference prices are stable authored values, not a promise that a finite local market will buy everything.

Starter goods and operational grants have positive reference value where appropriate but zero historical paid basis. FIFO paid basis is not added again to Company Value. Moving goods between owned stores neither creates value nor realizes a sale.

A ship is valued at 50 coins per whole capacity unit. Facilities use their authored replacement construction cost. A paid pending order is replaced by its completed asset at completion, without double counting. The public Mint, treasury, households and other companies are excluded.

Cash pays orders and wages now. Realized material margin is actual sale revenue less released FIFO material basis; operating surplus after wages also subtracts all paid wages, including wages for held output. Mint receipts, surrendered Silver basis and public commissions are shown separately. Company Value change is not realized profit or liquidation proceeds.

mechanics.name: Historical inventory cost
mechanics.description: Held goods carry actual acquisition or input-material expenditure through their journey.
paragraphs: Stock uses first-in, first-out acquisition lots in receipt order within each store and commodity. Several purchases at different prices remain distinguishable. A partial sale releases the earliest available slices at that store; transferred slices join the end of the destination queue with their original cost and provenance. Current market quotes never rewrite historical cost.

A lot's cost is allocated by exact cumulative integer shares. Taking a slice releases the difference between the cumulative shares at its end and start. Split transfers preserve that original interval, so slicing cannot manufacture or lose cost through rounding.

Production removes the historical material cost of its consumed inputs and allocates that total across actual output units in stable commodity order. Finished goods therefore carry their input-material cost. Transfers keep that cost without creating revenue.

Starter grants retain explicit grant provenance and zero purchased expenditure. That is not market value. Living Cities production wages are immediately expensed separately, not added to FIFO material basis. Depreciation, travel and other overhead remain unmodeled; zero material basis is not zero total economic cost.

mechanics.name: Fractional goods and exact coins
mechanics.description: V3 households buy proportional quantities while ships carry whole cargo units.
paragraphs: Expanding Economy v3 stores 10,000 physical subunits per good and 10,000 monetary subunits per coin. Displays format those integers; they never change balances. Canonical recipes execute complete batches at this scale. For example, consuming 0.75 Bread from a shelf holding 2.00 leaves exactly 1.25.

A ship order must be a whole cargo-unit quantity. With 2.75 Bread for sale, a ship can load at most two whole Bread and leaves 0.75. Household purchases and local private storage can retain fractional stock. Capacity counts the actual combined goods once.

Exact totals sum marginal inventory edges. Splitting an uninterrupted order across fractional boundaries has the same total as buying the combined quantity, while every debit equals its credit. The displayed average is informational. Unrepresentable amounts fail rather than wrap or disappear.

An authored population fraction finer than one physical subunit carries its exact residual numerator to the next due opportunity. Food observations retain actual desired, purchased, stock-short and funds-short quantities. Current and initial-population need have separate carry, so population decline cannot erase the recovery baseline.

mechanics.name: Expanding production chains
mechanics.description: Invest in real capacity and inspect the next finite bottleneck.
paragraphs: Every v3 world permits all six original production building types somewhere. Eligibility follows economic roles, not displayed city names. The food source can host Farms; the processing town can host Mills and Sawmills. The forest-furniture town can host a Silver Mine but cannot build a Sawmill, preserving a real Plank import dependency.

Each owned facility has a separate schedule, enabled state, policy and production/payroll counters. Each company shares one owned stockpile per town. Multiple Mills may coexist. Public and private extraction create only their declared batch outputs, and every successful living batch pays its full configured wage from the real employer.

An extra Mill expands potential Flour output. Actual results still require Grain, wages and warehouse space, then a Bakery with Flour and Logs, and actual distribution to households able to pay. Overbuilding can consume cash without improving food access. Distinguish a recorded last-attempt failure from current conditions before changing policy.

mechanics.name: Owning a factory
mechanics.description: Invest cash in a fixed recipe and a finite private stockpile.
paragraphs: The active scenario lists blueprints, eligible towns, construction payments, intervals and storage limits. Construction pays the local market once and creates empty owned storage. Ascension 0 is immediately operational; Ascension 1 new player sites complete after two economic days. The first batch is eligible one full production interval after completion, with inputs and capacity still required.

The industry summary shows status, next opportunity, missing inputs and local quotes, real expenditure and physical shipping waits. A recommended setup prepares a visible policy draft; only Apply commits it. Keep local output sales disabled, or retain an appropriate reserve, when a ship should transport finished goods. Detailed rules remain available.

A charter may grant an initial facility or goods. Those starter assets are grants, not purchases or construction payments during the run. Starter facilities are already operational at both ascensions and retain their initial schedule. Capital spending remains separate from material cost and sale margin.

Living Cities has town-specific construction eligibility. An industry may be absent and also impossible to build locally. Cash alone cannot override this restriction; use the eligible-town list and import missing inputs through real trades or shipping.

V3 makes Farms, Lumber Camps, Mills, Sawmills, Bakeries, Furniture Workshops and Silver Mines constructible somewhere, with eligibility visible before purchase. Multiple separate sites of the same eligible kind are allowed. A second Mill still needs Grain, paid labor, storage and customers; no construction creates free inputs. The public Royal Mint is commissioned separately and is never a private blueprint.

In new v3 runs a local Mill deposits Flour into the same owned town stock used by a Bakery. Facilities execute in stable port/ID order; an earlier eligible batch can consume scarce inputs before another. Only successful batches pay wages. Procurement targets and output reserves use current shared stock, so disable or reserve output sales when another local recipe needs it.

mechanics.name: Financial reports and the ledger
mechanics.description: Separate cash, revenue, attributed costs, realized margin, and capital.
paragraphs: Sale revenue is actual money received. Cost of goods sold is the historical basis released by those sales. Realized gross margin is revenue minus that attributed cost. Unsold cargo and warehouse goods retain their basis instead of becoming realized profit.

Inventory purchases are cash outflows, while held inventory cost describes the purchased or manufactured goods still owned. Construction is separate capital spending, not another cargo purchase or a recurring charge on every manufactured unit.

The ledger identifies committed transactions, transfers, production, and grants with their company, store, commodity, quantity, time, and relevant cash or cost. The visible journal is bounded; authoritative lifetime summaries remain available after old detail entries leave the display.

Historical modes do not value ships and factories. Expanding Economy v3 adds a disclosed reference Company Value, not liquidation proceeds. Material gross margin remains revenue minus FIFO material cost. Living modes separately expense all actual wages: operating surplus after wages subtracts them, including wages for output still held. This is not full net profit after travel, depreciation, overhead or taxes.

Port service fees are separate from material FIFO and wages. Surplus after wages and fees subtracts both operating expenses from realized material margin; it excludes construction capital, Mint receipts and unmodeled costs. Fees are paid from actual sale proceeds, half to the local market and the remainder to local workers. Lifetime rounding is shared across the company's sales in each town.

mechanics.name: Commission and direct a fleet
mechanics.description: Up to three owned ships share cash but keep separate cargo and routes.
paragraphs: V3 permits the starting ship and two additional ships. The processing harbor shipwright charges 500 coins and consumes four real market Planks. Of that payment, 460 goes to the market and 40 to local households for labor. Construction takes four economic days; completion creates an empty ten-unit ship at that harbor.

Pending orders count toward the three-ship limit and retain paid capital in Company Value. Missing company cash or actual market Planks prevents the order without partial payment or a phantom ship. Private-factory Ascension timing is separate from this shipbuilding schedule.

Select the intended owned ship before trading, sailing, transfer or route editing. All ships share one company account, but each has its own cargo, position, policy and enabled state. New itineraries retain an exact stop/action/pass and daily budget; older industrial routes retain their original stage. Ships act in stable priority and ID order through one atomic day; one ship cannot load another ship's cargo.

Fleet mode lists owned ships beside the map and selected-ship inspector. Cargo, dock or ETA, route and next instruction or wait reason remain visible; Committed activity reveals the cursor, daily work budget and last reason. Route planner opens that ship's ordered Buy/Sell/Load/Unload editor; Company / shipwright opens purchases and public services. Inspection never changes route enablement, cargo, funds or time.

mechanics.name: The Grand Commission and Objectives Journal
mechanics.description: Read the seeded map, draft four mandatory goals, and track real economic accomplishments.
paragraphs: Grand Commission is the default scored Expanding Economy v3 choice. Review all four towns, actual sea routes and building capabilities first. Then choose one of three distinct cards in each of four rounds: Navigation/Fleet, Production/Industry, Markets/Commerce and Civic/Capital. Each category has four real candidates. Backtracking preserves offers and never advances time. Review all four selections before Begin.

All four selected cards must be satisfied together by day 180, with at least 100 liquid company coins. Completed visits and actual production are permanent evidence; signed net sales, current facilities, cash, Company Value and recent paid-food conditions can become unmet. Each card shows its least-complete condition rather than hiding a blocker behind an average.

A New Industry needs an operational private Mill and Bakery in different towns, with a funded completed batch in each exact site. A starter Bakery beside the Mill does not satisfy the distinct-town condition. Pending construction, missing inputs, unfunded payroll, public output and purchased stock are not private production.

Destination commerce counts your company's actual sales minus purchases of the named good at the named town, for ship and private warehouse market trades. Buying four Flour and reselling those four locally earns zero; a later buyback can reverse imported delivery credit. NPC trades, quotes and unsold cargo do not count. Navigation records actual owned-ship docks and arrivals; a new second ship must sail beyond its shipyard to earn its second visit.

The navigation choices require four visited towns, three named role towns, a second ship visiting two towns, or three towns plus a positive remote net sale. Industry choices require distinct-town funded Mill/Bakery batches, a Lumber Camp/Sawmill with four private Planks, a Sawmill/Workshop with two private Furniture, or two-town Bakeries with four private Bread. Commerce requires four net Bread, Planks or Flour at the resolved destination, or 100 coins in finite external contract receipts.

Civic choices require a company-commissioned public Mint and one physical Silver issuance; recovery-town food coverage of 80 percent across six recent opportunities plus prosperity 50; Company Value growth of 100 coins with 100 cash; or two funded public-works Planks plus six recent food opportunities at 60 percent. Food uses actual paid consumption against the greater current and initial-population need. Deliveries alone are not meals, and welfare may fall again.

Open Objectives from play, pause or results for compact current/target values, completion bars and Current/Cumulative markers. Cumulative evidence stays earned; current conditions can fall again. Each card's Details & blockers retains the full explanation, actual facility identifiers and reasons. Cash floor and deadline stay visible. Journal inspection pauses playback, and zero-clamped bars never erase a negative net balance.

Mission draft version 1 and its exact four resolved cards are part of run identity. The same seed keeps the same offers regardless of charter, pricing, Ascension or earlier choices, without changing the economic world. Save/Continue restores the current plan and progress exactly; Retry Same World starts that same commission fresh. Explicit reroll returns to a new preview.

mechanics.name: Market liquidity
mechanics.description: Stock and money are separate finite limits.
paragraphs: A town can have goods to sell but too little cash to buy your cargo. Your company likewise needs actual cash to procure inputs, buy cargo, or construct a facility.
A blocked automated sale keeps unsold cargo aboard and explains the wait. Lowering a price limit cannot create buyer cash. Nothing silently replenishes stock or funds.

Households pay exact retail prices from their separate finite cash account; municipal Plank use is unpaid own-use. Extraction creates goods, not money. Wages, retail, construction and trade transfer actual cash between named accounts.

mechanics.name: Commodity roles and twelve-day signals
mechanics.description: Read local production, input needs and possible trade destinations without forecasting stock.
paragraphs: Harbor marks each good Produces, Uses, Makes + uses or Trade only. Inspect Town market for public facilities and household/municipal needs; inspect Company warehouse for your local industrial recipes and owned stock. Current market bid/ask stays public in both views. Inspection is independent of the Ship cargo or Company warehouse trade destination.

Signed production, use and net share one window: the next 12 economic days, tomorrow through day +12 inclusive. Output and input totals assume each scheduled enabled operational batch succeeds. Overdue work gets one next-day opportunity followed by its usual interval, with no catch-up output. Disabled and pending sites remain visible as installed capability in the breakdown but do not contribute to enabled totals.

Blocked marks current input, payroll, storage or output limits; the row still shows conditional enabled potential. Even Ready from current state does not reserve materials or wages. Another local facility can consume shared inputs first. Net is potential enabled output minus recipe inputs and consumption needs, not a promised future inventory. No trade, procurement, automatic sale, ship transfer, voyage, contract or Mint flow is counted as passive production.

Household needs hold current population and luxury eligibility fixed, using the saved exact fractional demand carry. Need is not actual consumption. Select the good and open breakdown for per-facility schedules and blockers, next stock/affordability gaps and Last actual consumption, payment and unmet quantities. Before the first observation, the panel says so. Stock < need compares today's stock with gross window needs; production or imports can still cover the gap.

Open compare towns for the selected good's real public stock, current marginal bids/asks, finite market buying power and travel time from the selected ship's dock. Choosing a row inspects that town and retains the good. A price spread is a lead to investigate, not guaranteed profit or remote permission to move cargo. Exact bulk pricing, fees, finite cash and physical voyages still govern every order. Eligible construction remains in Industry.

mechanics.name: Map, command deck, pause and navigation
mechanics.description: Inspect, pause, and begin another run without accidentally advancing the economy.
paragraphs: Start from the main menu, choose New Run or unlimited Sandbox, then review the challenge, charter, Expanding Economy v3 map preview, and Ascension 0 or 1. Setup, seed editing and reference browsing do not advance economic time or reroll a started world.

Select a town or ship on Map to open the compact bottom command deck. Collapse or reopen it without changing the economy. Map, Trade, Industry, Fleet, Economy and Objectives are working modes. Trade and Industry reuse their existing controls; Fleet opens the selected owned ship's route planner; Economy leads to full city accounts and Ledger; Objectives opens the real Journal.

Switching modes and opening management views pauses playback. Inspection, route overlays and Back never trade, move stock, advance a day or enable automation. Harbor, Industry and planner return to their previous context with the relevant town and ship retained. Use Play or Next day deliberately; the pause menu's explicit Resume restores playback only if it was running when pause opened.

Escape respects the active confirmation or Harbor/Industry overlay first. It returns Fleet, Economy or a context chooser to Map, returns detailed screens to their parent, and opens pause from ordinary Map play. Details / log keeps the full Overview, Market and Controls inspector, activity and run identity. Company is reachable through pause or Fleet's Company / shipwright action.

Restart, abandonment, return to menu, and exit protect unsaved active progress with confirmation. Exit closes the standalone game. Save explicitly before leaving; Continue or Load restores a valid local saved run, while Retry Same World creates its initial state again.

The encyclopedia is available from the main menu, run setup, and pause menu. Browse a category, search names or descriptions, follow related entries, and use Back to return. All recipe facts are generated from the same content the simulation loads and work offline. Settings offers four game-wide text sizes without changing the world.

New Run defaults to Expanding Economy v3 and the Grand Commission. Advanced / Legacy keeps earlier worlds accessible, and Sandbox remains explicit. Inspect the large interactive map before drafting; invalid seed text leaves the last valid preview intact. Retry and Load preserve the original run identity.

mechanics.name: Company, market, and private ownership
mechanics.description: One company cash account supports distinct ship cargo and private warehouses.
paragraphs: A public market owns its stock. Buying from it changes ownership and moves cash. A factory's private stock belongs to its company and is separate from the town market, even when they occupy the same port.

Transfers between your ship and your warehouse preserve ownership and historical cost. They are not sales and move no cash or time. Both stores must have the same owner and the ship must be docked at the warehouse's town.
Remote management may buy or sell against a factory's local market. It cannot move goods to another port. Company cash shown beside a ship is the same account, not another balance.

Storage rules 2 give each company one town stockpile and one FIFO account shared by its local industries. Ships, public markets, other owners and other towns remain separate. Facility reports keep separate labor and production counters, never duplicate copies of the shared goods. Old saved runs retain storage rules 1 and their actual facility stores.

mechanics.name: Marginal prices and execution averages
mechanics.description: The displayed next price and the cost of a whole order answer different questions.
paragraphs: Ask is what you pay to buy; bid is what the market pays when you sell. In the regional scenario each unit changes public stock, so later units in a large order may have different prices.

The exact total adds the actual prices across the complete order. Average execution price is that total divided by quantity for display. Neither average nor the first marginal price replaces the exact total used for payment.

An automation price limit applies to the worst marginal unit in its selected order. A profitable-looking current quote does not guarantee the same price after a voyage, production, consumption, or another merchant's trade.

Modern circulation Coverage pricing protects Furniture with a two-good target floor even when luxury purchases are suspended. Actual stock and each town's reference price still determine bid and ask; the target creates neither demand nor goods.

Harbor's selected-good compare towns panel lists real current marginal bids/asks, public stock, buying power and travel days from the selected ship's dock. Select a town to inspect it without losing the good selection. Price differences do not guarantee a profitable shipment: exact bulk prices, sale fees, finite liquidity and changes during travel still apply.

mechanics.name: Private procurement and local sales
mechanics.description: Maintain chosen inputs and sell chosen surplus through ordinary local trades.
paragraphs: For each recipe input, choose a target stock and maximum marginal buying price. A cash reserve protects company liquidity. Procurement buys only what the local town can supply and the company can afford within the policy.

For outputs, choose a retained quantity and minimum marginal selling price. Surplus sales use the town's actual cash and the same exact pricing as manual trades. Each configured good gets at most one transaction in its daily policy phase.

Targets compete for shared cash and warehouse space. A price, liquidity, stock, or capacity wait is a real constraint. Policies never discover a substitute source or create resources to meet a target. Under-construction sites do not automatically procure or sell until the day after completion; explicitly managing their local stock remains possible.

mechanics.name: Production and scheduling
mechanics.description: Complete canonical recipes run at explicitly scheduled economic days.
paragraphs: A recipe lists its actual input and output quantities. Transformation requires every input. Extraction has no tradeable inputs and creates its configured output. Canonical recipe pages describe quantities; the active scenario supplies intervals and limits.

A private factory consumes and produces only within its actual owned store: a shared company town stockpile in pooled runs, or its separate warehouse in older runs. Public market goods never silently supply a private batch. A successful batch schedules the next opportunity one interval later. Missing inputs, disabled production or full output storage keep the batch due without accumulating catch-up batches.

Daily ship actions occur before procurement and production. Operational private procurement is followed by public production, private production, private sales, scheduled consumption, voyage progress and due construction completion. Fresh output cannot be loaded by an earlier ship action in that same daily operation. Pending factories skip their automatic phases even on completion day.

In Living Cities, a successful public batch pays the configured wage from market cash to local households; a private batch pays from its company. Insufficient payroll blocks the whole batch and keeps it due. Blocked, disabled, input-starved and pending batches pay nothing. After retail, city observations and population reviews occur before voyages and construction completion.

Economy keeps each facility's recipe, readiness and next eligible day visible. Expand Inputs, payroll & last outcome for current stock, employer funds, wage, capacity, output ceiling and previous attempt. Ready from current state is conditional: earlier operations or another facility can use shared inputs first. Open Industry to manage an owned facility; inspecting the signal never runs a batch.

mechanics.name: Text size and readable controls
mechanics.description: Choose one presentation scale for every ArchipelagoLab screen.
paragraphs: Settings offers Compact, Default, Large and Extra Large text throughout gameplay, map labels, trade, industry, automation, ledger, encyclopedia, setup, pause and results. Default body text is 17 pixels; Large and Extra Large use 21 and 25. Compact uses 14 for a deliberately denser presentation.

The map keeps the main play area while a collapsible parchment command deck shows the selected town or ship. Dedicated Fleet and Economy workspaces expose focused facts; Details / log retains longer inspector details. Panels wrap and scroll internally where text grows. Buttons, numeric fields and hit targets adjust with text rather than using paint-only zoom; long documents and advanced configuration intentionally retain scrolling.

Goods and status symbols keep visible labels or tooltips; warnings use words as well as color. HUD cash and reference value use at most one decimal, with an exact tooltip; a positive value below 0.1 appears as <0.1. Harbor totals and Ledger money keep exact precision. Display rounding never changes an order, affordability or score.

Changing text size is passive: it does not advance time, change revision, spend cash, alter rules or reroll a seed. The text preference is remembered locally through Unity PlayerPrefs for the application environment, across menus and fresh runs. Other presentation settings last for the session. This does not save an economic run or synchronize preferences between devices.

mechanics.name: External trade and the public Royal Mint
mechanics.description: Finite outside purchases import cash; bounded Silver-backed issuance creates it.
paragraphs: The external authority has one visible finite account. A contract specifies goods, whole-unit quantity, harbor, payment and deadline. You must own and physically deliver its cargo there. Delivered goods leave the region; payment moves existing authority cash into the company. Completed quantities and spent funds never refill on expiry.

Exactly one processing-role harbor hosts the public Royal Mint. Commissioning pays the treasury once and starts its explicit construction delay. The institution belongs to the region and never counts as Company Value. The Silver Mine is in a different role, requiring real shipping.

An active ready Mint accepts one physically delivered Silver from the selected docked owned ship. That metal enters the public reserve and cannot be used twice. The authored batch creates 80 coins, paying 60 to the supplier and 20 to the treasury, with four days between batches and at most 24 batches. Silver material basis and Mint receipts remain separate from ordinary sale margin.

The treasury can buy a bounded real quantity of delivered Planks only while funded. Commission and minted public shares are actual treasury funds, not an unlimited credit line. Regional cash counts markets, households, companies and treasury. All-account cash also counts the outside authority. Only recorded Mint issuance increases all-account money.

Bread and Furniture purchases move existing household cash to markets and consume actual goods. Neither creates nor destroys coins. Extra money cannot replace missing Grain, Flour, Logs, employers or voyages.

mechanics.name: Save, Continue and exact retry
mechanics.description: Local explicit saves preserve an economic run; retry starts its identity fresh.
paragraphs: Save explicitly to one of three local slots. Continue or Load restores a current Expanding Economy v3 Grand Commission or Sandbox run without advancing time. Saves are local; there is no cloud recovery.

Only current schema5, circulation1, storage2 and itinerary1 are supported. Historical prototype saves are intentionally unsupported during pre-release development. No migration or command replay is performed.

Saves retain exact identity and drafted goals, accounts, fractional stock and demand residuals, FIFO lots, every voyage and route cursor/budget, pending construction, household history, fees, contracts, Mint and public treasury. Terminal outcomes remain frozen.

Complete validation precedes session replacement. Unsupported versions, damage or inconsistent state show an error and preserve the active world, selection and playback. Retry starts the original identity fresh. Text size remains an independent preference.

mechanics.name: Results and scoring
mechanics.description: Read the explicit score breakdown alongside the actual economy.
paragraphs: Results identify the complete run, outcome, day, four objective cards, company cash, reference value and attributed accounts. Compare only matching seed, charter, difficulty, pricing, rules and exact drafted commission.

Each card uses its least-complete condition percentage, capped between0 and100. Objective points equal floor(500 times the sum of four card percentages divided by400). Victory still requires all four goals and100 liquid coins.

Victory adds1000 points, remaining deadline days add10 each capped at600, and each10 liquid company coins adds one solvency point capped at100. Fractions round down; total score is at most2200. Transaction counts earn no extra points.

mechanics.name: Seeded worlds and exact retries
mechanics.description: Inspect the seeded economic map and retry the exact current run identity.
paragraphs: Current runs use Expanding Economy v3. Enter an ASCII signed integer from-2147483648 through2147483647, without spaces or separators. The same seed retains exact geography and role draws; no world is repaired after observing strategy performance.

Pure integer geography uses four separated jittered slots and six integer ceiling-square-root distances. A separate bounded stream permutes food supply, processing, forest furniture and vulnerable coast roles. Forest furniture needs imported Planks because it cannot build a Sawmill.

Identity includes seed, generator/content3, valuation1, pricing, charter, Ascension, objective draft, storage2, itinerary1 and circulation1. Retry restores this original initial world. Loading restores a saved position.

Randomize or Reroll explicitly chooses another draft seed, shows the preview and waits for a separate start. Menus and inspection never reroll. Structural production paths do not guarantee perpetual solvency or victory.

mechanics.name: Shipping and voyages
mechanics.description: Goods travel aboard a real ship between directly connected towns.
paragraphs: Departing changes the ship's voyage immediately without spending a day. Advancing economic days progresses travel. After arrival is committed, manual dockside actions are available at the destination.

Duration follows the route's distance and the ship's configured speed. Seeded geography derives all six direct distances from the generated integer positions. Distances are abstract chart units, not coastline-aware sailing paths. Map drawing and playback speed never alter travel or economic calculations. You cannot trade or transfer while sailing.

There are currently no simulated ship-crew wages, fuel, voyage fees or transport losses. Living Cities models production wages only. Unmodeled transport expenditure is not a claim that shipping has no real economic cost.

mechanics.name: Buying and selling
mechanics.description: Exchange goods with a town using the company's finite cash account.
paragraphs: Buy follows Market → Ship or Market → Warehouse and pays the town. Sell follows Ship → Market or Warehouse → Market; the market pays your company less the sale fee. Ship orders require the actual local dock. Company warehouse trades can be managed remotely, but goods remain at that town.

Choose a good and quantity, then read the exact order total before confirming. Manual trades execute the complete requested quantity or leave goods and cash unchanged. Quantity shortcuts only edit the proposal. Transactions do not advance the economic day.

Select a town or owned ship, then use Harbor on its command deck or the Trade mode. Without a selection, Trade offers a town chooser. Opening Harbor pauses playback; closing it returns to the previous context and stays paused. Disable that ship's automation before issuing manual trades or sailing orders.

Harbor separates Inspect (Town market or Company warehouse) from Trade with (Ship cargo or Company warehouse). Inspection scope never changes the order destination. Load follows Warehouse → Ship; Unload follows Ship → Warehouse. Both need the real dock and move no cash. Exact previews and blockers explain which paid or no-cash action can execute.

New modern v3 circulation runs charge 2% port handling on completed company sales, including NPC sales. Harbor shows the gross market payment, exact fee, net receipts and local market/worker shares. Buying, private transfers and public contracts have no handling fee. Rejected orders and previews charge nothing.
